P1.evidence: The rep started a setter read-back — "I know you spoke, ooh, I believe you spoke with Kim, right?... He gave me a..." — and was immediately diverted into the Sophia conversation, never returning to it. The frame was the usual reduced version, though better articulated than most: "You get a good idea of where you're at. Go probably in more depth about what it is that you want. Everything that we do is reverse engineered around the outcome. So we'll go deep on that. And then if there's alignment, we can talk about it." Agreement was assumed from "Okay, right. Cool" rather than asked for. The open question ran: "What are you hoping we could help you with now?"

P2.evidence: Among the better baselines in the batch. Height and weight were asked directly — "How much do you weigh and how tall are you?" — producing 5'10" and a few pounds north of 200, though age was volunteered rather than asked. Work was asked at the top ("What do you do?") and the desk-bound nature emerged. Training week was fully mapped: four mornings, wife takes three, no swaps allowed. Diet was asked properly ("What's your food like, nutrition-wise? What kind of stuff do you eat?") and produced the fasting protocols, including a 77-hour water fast. What is missing is the health half: no health-conditions question at all, and the limitations question was asked only in mobility terms ("Flexibility-wise, are there any specific areas you're noticing which you're like, ah, this isn't up to scratch?"). Sleep was never asked despite being one of the prospect's own stated goals — he volunteered two and a half years of poor sleep unprompted, which the script counts as a miss. Energy likewise.

P3.evidence: The best goals work in the batch. "When was the last time you didn't have the marshmallow?" opened a real history. The six-month question was asked and answered concretely (mirror, sub-185, flexibility, sleep). The bridge was asked properly and in the right place: "for you, I guess, what do you feel like changes when you get to that point for you? Like, what is that that you're searching for behind all of that?" — and it produced the actual why, unprompted and in the prospect's own words: "I like picking up my kids and throwing them around... I do a couple of those, and I'm gassed, right? So I need to keep up with them." The reflect-back was excellent and the correction it drew proves it worked: "Six months, notable difference in the mirror, looking better, confidence, take your shirt off, more agile, more flexible, better sleep, 185" — "Yeah. I would say 180." What was still not asked: 'who else does that impact', and the drive-through to kids and legacy was affirmed only after the fact ("the people who always have kids and the motivation is the kids get the best results") rather than built during discovery.

P4.evidence: The weakest phase on a strong call. Past attempts surfaced as anecdote rather than inquiry — Body for Life in his twenties, the 2020 Dopey Challenge — and the rep never asked why any of it stopped working. The prospect handed him the whole phase in one line at 00:17:40: "if I was diligent, I probably wouldn't be on this call right now. So, you know, sometimes you just need a kick in the ass." The rep's reply was "yeah, I hear ya" and a change of subject. The root cause was named again later, still unprompted — "once I run the event, then I just kind of take a week or two off, but that week or two turns into like three or four" — and again went unexplored. Nothing was asked about what gets in the way, nothing let him name the gap, and the 'information isn't the problem' line was never run.

P5.evidence: Not run. No two-year question, no 'willing to settle', no 'why not', no line in the sand. This is the most striking omission in the batch because the material was already on the table and the prospect had said it himself: 46 years old, three children under nine, gassed after two lifts, "I can't be a good dad if I'm dead" and "I either need to be fitter or I need a DeLorean." Two years forward from there writes itself. The rep's response was to agree warmly ("it's beautiful, it's a good why") and move to the pitch.

P6.evidence: No commitment check before presenting. The belief question was never asked in any form. The nearest thing to the all-in question came an hour in, after the price and after the tier decision: "Was there anything you wanted to go over or were you kind of ready to rock?" — a soft close, not a commitment gate. The prospect closed himself on his own motivation ("I'm fired up to do stuff now"), which is exactly the scenario the phase is meant to make unnecessary to rely on.

P11.evidence: Steps 1 and 2 ran and in the right order — the rep was explicit that payment precedes onboarding ("We process the investment and stuff and get you all set up now and then book that call in") and the prospect confirmed the sequence ("Oh, so I pay and then talk to Trevor? Yeah, yeah"). Card confirmed as Visa, onboarding booked for 3:15pm the next day. Step 3 was not run at all: no agreement email, nothing signed on the call. Step 4 got a single glancing reference — "I just want to make sure you have all the resources and access to your onboarding form" — with no welcome email, no Skool community link and no instruction to complete the questionnaire before the Trevor call.

objection_plays.detail: Not a classic 'think about it' — the deliberation was between six and twelve months, not whether to buy: "I gotta kind of sit and do the math. I'm neurotically analytical." His reasoning was sound and self-aware (he falls off after events, so a longer commitment might protect him). The rep did not explore that at all. He collapsed the decision with a commercial claim instead: a further six months would cost $3,000, not $6,000, so the twelve-month tier carries no discount. The prospect repeated it back to confirm and chose six immediately. Effective, and it moved the deal from $9,000 to $6,000, but it rests on a renewal price nobody on the call could verify. See the flags file.

"I have no idea what my kettlebell access will be like on my vacation" plus "I could technically start on the 22nd. Is that an option?" The rep did not run the play and did not need to — he offered a bodyweight bridge or a pause with the time credited back, and the prospect argued himself out of the delay: "I don't really like delaying starting though when I'm motivated to do something." The rep supported it with the right instinct ("the thing when it comes to any change you make in your life is making the decision to commit") but none of the scripted moves appeared.

Script gap with real exposure. The prospect challenged the identity of the entity that had been texting him: "the text chain with, allegedly, Sophia, who I'm not convinced is AI." There is no scripted handling for a prospect asking whether they have been talking to a person. The rep chose disclosure, which was the right call and he made it immediately — "I'll be super transparent with you. Sophia's AI" — but then volunteered that the system is designed to avoid detection ("Sophia is typically pretty good at, you know, not causing any suspicion"). The playbook needs a position on this, because the next prospect may not be as relaxed as this one.

Second gap: the prospect's stated outcome included "better sleep" and two and a half years of poor sleep, which none of the three pillars formally covers. The rep handled it personally and generously, offering to send his own materials free and mentioning he had paid a sleep coach $10,000 — but that is a salesperson improvising around a chronic health complaint, and it also happens to be the sharpest supports_price anchor on the call being spent on a giveaway rather than on the offer.

notes: Textbook goals work — the reflect-back that got corrected from 185 to 180, and the bridge that surfaced the kids — sitting on top of no root cause, no consequence frame and no commitment check. The prospect said 'sometimes you just need a kick in the ass' out loud and the rep let it pass, then closed on the prospect's own momentum. Coach the middle of the call: this deal was available at $9,000 and closed at $6,000 on a renewal-price promise that should not be made on a call at all.
